# LocalGPT for LLMs

LocalGPT is a .NET 10 Blazor/ASP.NET Core application hosted inside a WinUI 3 WebView2 Windows wrapper. It uses DevExpress Blazor components, Ollama-hosted AI models, configuration-driven AI profile selection, and backend services for native command execution and Minecraft mod workspace automation.

Main projects:

- LocalGPTWebviewWrapper/LocalGPT: ASP.NET Core host, Blazor UI, DevExpress components, AI services, setup/configuration pages, SQLite chat memory, AI Council, and Minecraft workspace builder.
- LocalGPTWebviewWrapper/LocalGPTWebviewWrapper: WinUI 3 and WebView2 desktop shell.
- LocalGPTWebviewWrapper/LocalGPTWebviewWrapper (Package): MSIX/DesktopBridge package project for deploy/debug.
- LocalGPTWebviewWrapper/build: repair/build scripts for local Windows development.

Key architecture:

- the WinUI wrapper should stay thin
- Blazor/server code owns AI, configuration, and command orchestration
- DevExpress static assets require LocalGPT.staticwebassets.runtime.json in the packaged executable folder
- native commands should flow through backend services such as INativeCommandRunner

Important assumptions:

- Visual Studio MSBuild is required for full package validation
- .NET 10 is the current target; `global.json` pins SDK 10.0.300 with latest-feature roll-forward
- loose AppX deploy needs image assets under bin/<platform>/<configuration>/AppX/Images; 0x80070002, 0x80073CF9, or DEP1000 can mean stale LocalGPT registration or missing manifest images
- DevExpress 25.1 packages are expected
- Ollama runs outside the app and is selected/configured through setup data
- preferred Ollama debug model is gpt-oss:20b
- run LocalGPTWebviewWrapper/build/Test-OllamaGptOss.ps1 before debugging DxAIChat
- Minecraft Builder should let the user/council choose Fabric mod, NeoForge mod, Paper plugin, vanilla datapack, or future Bedrock add-on
- use LocalGPTWebviewWrapper/build/Setup-MinecraftModToolchain.ps1 for JDK, Gradle, Eclipse, and Minecraft builder setup checks
- use /__diag/dxaichat-smoke for configured DXAiChat backend tests and /__diag/council for council tests before falling back to direct Ollama
- use /__diag/minecraft/datapack-benchmark?minecraftVersion=1.21.4 for the Living Cities datapack benchmark; it creates a validated zip and a compact CouncilKnowledgeEntries record for later model review
- use /__diag/logs to inspect SQLite application warnings/errors; AI bootstrap includes recent log health signals for DXAiChat and council runs
- after black screens or high GPU pressure, use database-first low-resource council settings: one model, MaxRounds 0, MaxOutputTokens 256 or less, MaxContextTokens 2048, OllamaKeepAlive "0s", OllamaNumGpu 0, then check ollama ps before/after
- AI Council conversations saved in SQLite can be continued through ContinueConversationId or the frontend memory selector; every step should show the full council roster
- faulty council members may be excluded by the user, but models should request that through a poll instead of silently excluding peers
- implementation-request council chats can ask LocalGPT to generate a downloadable CodeDOM C# starter artifact for .NET/Blazor/ASP.NET Core ideas
- use /__diag/devexpress before proposing DevExpress APIs; Office/report/PDF/file generation belongs in ASP.NET Core backend services with safe download endpoints
- use /__diag/build-debug-files for .pdb/.pdg/.appxsym symbol inventory, but do not confuse symbol/reference presence with source-level feature usage
- requested features should be prototyped in harmless sandbox artifacts or temporary workspaces before integration into the real project
- never self-expand LocalGPT or integrate generated features without explicit user permission; never overrule a user decision that denies or limits expansion
- missing-feature reports should include helpful sources requested by AI participants, without claiming those sources were verified
- use LOCALGPT_WEBVIEW2_SMOKE=1 in the WinUI wrapper to capture WebView2 page snapshots for desktop-shell validation. Prefer this fallback over an agent built-in browser when testing LocalGPT frontend usability, because it exercises the real WinUI/WebView2 wrapper and route flow.
